subject: Mutual Action Plan: Deployment mode & region decision for Enterprise Pay
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@enterprise-pay.com>, Oliver Barnes <oliver.barnes@enterprise-pay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP proposal — deployment mode & region decision for Enterprise Pay

Hi Samira / Oliver —

Thanks again for the meeting earlier. As discussed, I’m attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan that captures the evaluation plan, Milestones, and the decision point we need on deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and region. High-level proposal:

- Pilot: Hosted (US-EAST) — low-friction to get telemetry and functional validation (2 weeks)
- Evaluation: Run PoC traffic pattern, measure p99 latency and token usage across sample workloads (2 weeks)
- Production decision: Dedicated capacity in US-EAST for PCI-compliant payments flows, with Hosted fallback for burst (target prod cutover by 2026-04-05)

Key asks from Enterprise Pay to finalize MAP:
1) Confirm expected QPS and 95/99th percentile latency SLOs for the payment flows
2) Confirm whether data residency requires on-prem or VPC-private deployment (you mentioned US-only residency)
3) Procurement timeline for signed commitment or reserved capacity (we can convert the pilot to reserved Dedicated capacity once you commit)

Attachments: MAP-EnterprisePay-v3.pdf (draft milestones), SLA-term-sheet.xlsx (pricing/discount scenarios).

If this looks right I’ll circulate an updated MAP with specific milestone dates and add Lauren and Dev to the evaluation checklist.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--
From: Samira Khan <samira@enterprise-pay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Barnes <oliver.barnes@enterprise-pay.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MAP proposal — deployment mode & region decision for Enterprise Pay

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear proposal. A few clarifications from our side:
- We want to run the pilot on Hosted in US-EAST to accelerate validation, but production will need Dedicated capacity in US-EAST due to PCI and our compliance team’s preference for isolated pools.
- Expected steady QPS for the initial rollout: ~80 requests/s (mostly short prompts, average 120 tokens/request). Peak burst to 300 requests/s for reconciliation windows.
- Latency targets: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 450ms for payment-affecting flows.
- Procurement: procurement is aggressive — we need signed terms by 2026-04-01 to meet our internal quarter close.

I’m uploading the partially completed security questionnaire separately (security-questionnaire-filled.pdf).

If you can put the MAP milestones with explicit dates (pilot start, PoC end, reserved capacity commit date) that will help us align procurement and engineering.

—Samira
Head of Product Risk | Enterprise Pay

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2026 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP proposal — deployment mode & region decision for Enterprise Pay

Rishi / Lauren —

Quick engineering note on Dedicated provisioning and the evaluation plan:
- We can provision a Dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1; estimated lead time is 3–4 weeks from signed commit for reserved capacity to be ready for production traffic.
- For the pilot, Hosted in us-east will give us real telemetry. We recommend enabling KV-caching for the payment flows and a 50ms batching window for reconciliation burst traffic to reduce cost.
- Constraints: if Enterprise Pay needs strict BYOK/HSM integration for keys, that adds ~1 week of integration testing with KMS.

Action items for the PoC checklist (engineering):
- Provide sample workloads / representative tokens by Mar 12
- Enable tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown in the pilot
- Run load profile to validate p99 latency at expected QPS

I’ll slot time on 3/15 for a short tech sync if Samira/Oliver want to walk through infra requirements.

—Dev
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

--
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@enterprise-pay.com>, Oliver Barnes <oliver.barnes@enterprise-pay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP proposal — deployment mode & region decision for Enterprise Pay

Samira / Oliver —

Thanks — sounds like we have alignment. Proposed MAP milestones with dates below (please confirm):
1) Pilot kickoff (Hosted, us-east): 2026-03-22 — 2 weeks functional and telemetry testing
2) PoC evaluation & perf validation: 2026-04-05 — measure p95/p99, token spend, failover tests
3) Reserved commit for Dedicated capacity (target): 2026-04-05 — commit required to hit prod cutover 2026-04-29
4) Production cutover (Dedicated, us-east): 2026-04-29 — with Hosted fallback for bursts

Notes: Dev called out BYOK/HSM work (if required) and we’ll include that in the tech checklist. I’m also attaching the SLA-term-sheet.xlsx with the reserved capacity pricing and two discount tiers. Lauren — can you confirm internal onboarding tasks / PM owner?

If Enterprise Pay confirms the timeline we’ll:
- Lock the pilot start date and open a HubSpot milestone (link below)
- Send over a DocuSign with the MAP acknowledgement and the reserved capacity term sheet

Cheers,
Rishi

--

Quick commercial: if Enterprise Pay signs an annual reserved capacity commitment by 2026-04-01, we can extend a 15% reserved-capacity discount and include enterprise onboarding (one week dedicated support) and a 99.9% SLA. Please highlight procurement’s approval window to the customer — that is the gating item.

Also flagging legal: we’ll need the signed security questionnaire and any additional data residency language before we finalize the Dedicated contract. Samira — thanks for sending the partially completed questionnaire.

—Hannah
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

- Procurement: we will aim to sign by 2026-04-01 to make the discount window — procurement lead is Aaron Price (aaron.price@enterprise-pay.com).
